data.summary: The plan front‑loads the weak Unit 4 and then moves through the curriculum unit by unit, using the scheduled live classes when they occur. Each week balances 6 hours of focused study, concrete practice tasks, and review of earlier material. The final two weeks are dedicated to mixed review and timed practice to consolidate knowledge before the exam.

weeks.focus: Introduce chemical reactions and begin weak Unit 4.
tasks: Read the textbook sections 4.1‑4.3 and take concise notes.
Do 15 practice problems on identifying reactants/products and writing net ionic equations.
Check answers with the solution guide and correct any misconceptions.

weeks.focus: Atomic structure basics and start Unit 1.
tasks: Watch the live Class 9700 recording and answer the in‑class poll questions.
Complete 10 free‑response questions on moles and molar mass, grading with the scoring rubric.
Create a one‑page summary chart comparing mass spectroscopy and photoelectron spectroscopy.
Attend live Class 9701 and take notes on bond types and potential energy curves.
Draw Lewis structures for 8 different molecules, checking formal charges each time.
Complete a worksheet on predicting bond polarity and intermolecular forces.

weeks.focus: Intermolecular forces (Unit 3) and reinforce reaction basics (Unit 4).
tasks: Participate in both live classes (9702 & 9703) and answer the breakout‑room questions.
Complete 12 short‑answer questions comparing intermolecular forces in solids vs. liquids.
Redo 5 net‑ionic equation problems from Week 1, this time explaining each step aloud.

weeks.focus: Reaction rates and introductory kinetics – Unit 5.
tasks: Watch Class 9704 and fill in the provided rate‑law worksheet.
Calculate reaction rates for 6 different experiments using given concentration‑time data.
Sketch concentration‑vs‑time graphs for first‑order and zero‑order reactions.
Join live Class 9705 and complete the in‑class calorimetry problem set.
Solve 8 enthalpy change problems using Hess’s law and energy‑diagram interpretation.
Create flashcards for endothermic vs. exothermic processes and quiz yourself.
Attend Class 9706 and work through the equilibrium constant derivation together with peers.
Complete a set of 10 equilibrium‑quotient calculations, checking each with the answer key.
Write a one‑page summary explaining Le Chatelier’s principle with real‑world examples.

weeks.focus: Mixed review and timed practice – focus on Units 1‑5.
tasks: Take a 45‑minute timed free‑response practice test covering Units 1‑5.
Mark the test using the AP scoring guidelines and note any recurring errors.
Review flashcards for key equations (ideal gas law, rate law, stoichiometry) and redo the problematic questions.

weeks.focus: Comprehensive mixed review and full‑length timed practice.
tasks: Watch the recorded Class 9708 for a quick refresher on entropy and free energy.
Complete a 90‑minute full‑length AP Chemistry practice exam under timed conditions.
Score the exam, calculate your overall percentage, and write a brief action plan for the final days before the test.

data.final_week_advice: In the days leading up to 2026‑11‑03, focus on brief daily reviews of your flashcards, practice a few timed free‑response questions each day, and get plenty of rest. Trust the systematic work you’ve done each week and enter the exam confident.
